'''Sigma Zeta''' ('''{{lang|grc|ΣΖ}}''') is a North American [[honor society]] founded in 1925 to recognize undergraduate excellence in the [[natural science]]s, [[computer science]], and [[mathematics]]. The society's purpose is to encourage and foster the attainment of knowledge in the natural and computer sciences and mathematics.<ref>[http://sigmazeta.org/handbook "Introduction to the ''Sigma Zeta Handbook''"], Sigma Zeta. retrieved 2013-11-11</ref> It has chartered more than eighty chapters in the United States and Canada.

==History==
Sigma Zeta was founded in the fall of 1925 at the now defunct [[Shurtleff College]] in [[Alton, Illinois]] as a local coeducational organization to provide recognition for Shurtleff science and mathematics students.<ref name=":0">{{Bairds17|pages=699-700}}</ref> Its founders were Professor Elmer E. List of the biology department, J. Ellis Powell of the math department; and Ralph K. Calteton, of the chemistry department.<ref name=":0" /> They selected the name Sigma Zeta and drafted a constitution and initiation ceremony on October 1, 1925.<ref name=":0" />

A second chapter, ''Beta'', was chartered at McKendree College in 1926.<ref name=":0" /> The society held its first conclave in June 1926.<ref name=":0" />

Soon after that other local campuses took an interest in the group, and following the approval of the petition by [[McKendree University|McKendree College]] to start a chapter in June 1926 Sigma Zeta began its growth into a national collegiate honor society.<ref>[http://sigmazeta.org/history "The History of Sigma Zeta"], Sigma Zeta. retrieved 2013-11-11</ref> In a letter that appeared in the correspondence section of the [[American Chemical Society]] ''[[Journal of Chemical Education]]'' Sigma Zeta was offered as an alternative for small colleges to the existing [[Sigma Xi]] honor society which often passed over small colleges for membership as they focused on larger Universities.<ref>[http://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdfplus/10.1021/ed003p944.2 R. K. Carrelton. "Correspondence."] ''Journal of Chemical Education'' 1926, 3 (8), p. 944</ref>

Sigma Zeta's annual convention has been held every year since 1926 except for 1943, 1944, and 1945 when it was canceled due to [[World War II]], and in 2020 when it was canceled due to the COVID-19 Pandemic.<ref>[http://sigmazeta.org/convention-history "Sigma Zeta Conventions Future and Past"], Sigma Zeta, retrieved 2013-11-11</ref> The first three gatherings were held at the Shurtleff College campus which is now the site of the [[Southern Illinois University School of Dental Medicine]].

Sigma Zeta became an international organization in 2024 with the chartering of a ''Gamma Phi chapter'' at [[St. Mary's University (Calgary)|St. Mary’s University]] in [[Calgary, Alberta]], Canada.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chapter Roll |url=https://sigmazeta.org/chapter-roll/ |access-date=2024-12-13 |website=Sigma Zeta}}</ref>

==Symbols==
Sigma Zeta's badge is a gold key, shaped like an open book,  with the Greek letters '''{{lang|grc|ΣΖ}}''' above various scientific symbols.<ref name=":0" /> The associate member's pin is blue and white enamel, with the Greek letters '''{{lang|grc|ΣΖ}}'''.<ref name=":0" />

The colors of Sigma Zeta are blue and white.<ref name=":0" /> Its publication is ''The Sigma Zetan''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sigma Zetan |url=https://sigmazeta.org/sigma-zetan/ |access-date=2024-12-13 |website=Sigma Zeta}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

==Activities==

The annual convention is Sigma Zeta's primary meeting where student members present papers and individual and chapter awards are presented.<ref>[http://www.malone.edu/news-and-events/press/6312.sigma.zeta.php Malone University to Host 2012 Sigma Zeta National Convention] (March 21, 2012). retrieved 2012-8-26</ref><ref>[http://www.ollusa.edu/s/1190/ollu.aspx?sid=1190&gid=1&pgid=6318&cid=8907&ecid=8907&ciid=68979&crid=0 OLLU to host national Sigma Zeta convention this Saturday] Our Lady of the Lake University (March 2011). retrieved 2012-8-26</ref><ref>[http://theaviso.org/2012/04/10/students-gather-from-across-nation-for-sigma-zeta-conference/ Students gather from across nation for Sigma Zeta conference], ''The Aviso'' (April 10, 2012). retrieved 2012-8-26</ref> Individual chapters often undertake activities including the hosting of speakers and service projects to benefit their local communities.<ref>[http://www.malone.edu/news-and-events/press/6283.nasa.speaker.php NASA Speaker Addresses Waves] Malone University (February 21, 2012). retrieved 2012-8-26</ref> These activities can include programs for younger students at local schools helping to promote science education at early ages.<ref>[http://www.asbury.edu/academics/departments/natural-sciences/news/2011-03-kids-college-explores-wonders-science Kid's College Explores Wonders of Science], Asbury University (March 11, 2011). retrieved 2012-8-27</ref><ref>[http://www.wcs.k12.va.us/articles/2010/12/08/john-s-battle-travels-to-sigma-zeta-math-and-science-competition John S. Battle Travels to Sigma Zeta Math and Science Competition] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20121224132131/http://www.wcs.k12.va.us/articles/2010/12/08/john-s-battle-travels-to-sigma-zeta-math-and-science-competition |date=2012-12-24 }}, Washington County Public Schools: Virginia (December 8th, 2012). retrieved 2012-8-27</ref>

In 1947, the three Sigma Zeta members presented the Founders Cup which is awarded to a chapter at each annual convention for papers presented.<ref name=":0" />

Sigma Zeta's interdisciplinary nature has been described as a benefit for smaller colleges and universities because, "It brings together students from all areas of science and mathematics, including computer science, so they can all work together on projects."<ref>[http://reflector.uindy.edu/2009/09/23/honor-societies-provide-benefits-prestige/ Honor societies provide benefits, prestige], ''The Reflector Online'' (September 23rd, 2009) retrieved 2012-8-27</ref>

==Membership==
Chapters select students for membership who have met the following eligibility criteria:
* Major studies in at least one of the Natural Sciences, Computer Science, or Mathematics
* Completion of 25 semester hours of coursework with 15 hours in the Natural Sciences, Computer Science, or Mathematics
* A [[Grading in education|Grade Point Average]] of 3.0 out of 4.0 both in Science and Mathematics as well as cumulatively among all classes taken<ref>[http://sigmazeta.org/membership "Why be a member of Sigma Zeta"], Sigma Zeta. retrieved 2013-11-11</ref>
